docs.title: Vitrify
docs.text:
vitrify turns a mutable SPARQL response into a durable, inspectable local file with its query and retrieval evidence.

  • SPARQL endpoint

    Send the exact query to Wikidata's mutable endpoint.

    https://query.wikidata.org/sparql

  • Vitrify command

    Capture five EU-capital labels in a local RO-Crate.

    echo 'PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?label
WHERE {
  ?country wdt:P463 wd:Q458 ;
           wdt:P36 ?capital .
  ?capital rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
ORDER BY ?label
LIMIT 5' |
  vitrify sparql \
  --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query - \
  --format csv \
  --to eu-capitals

  • RO-Crate directory

    The ordinary response file is kept with the exact query and RO-Crate evidence.

    eu-capitals/ ├── results.csv ├── ro-crate-metadata.json └── query.rq

docs.text: To vitrify is to turn something into glass. See also: Stanislaw Lem Fiasco.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: cargo install vitrify

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Vitrify currently provides the sparql command only. It sends one query to a SPARQL endpoint and saves the response body in an output directory.

vitrify sparql \
  --endpoint https://query.wikidata.org/sparql \
  --query docs/examples/female-persons/query.rq \
  --format csv \
  --to female-persons

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
Argument Required Description --endpoint IRI Yes SPARQL endpoint URL. --query PATH or --query - Yes Read the query from a UTF-8 file, or read standard input when the value is -. --to DIRECTORY Yes Directory for the result and its RO-Crate files. --format FORMAT No Request a response format; also supplies a fallback filename extension.

The query must not be empty. Standard input is read only when --query - is specified. Vitrify saves the query text it sends as query.rq in the output directory.

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
--format Requested media type Fallback extension json application/sparql-results+json .json xml application/sparql-results+xml .xml csv text/csv .csv tsv text/tab-separated-values .tsv turtle text/turtle .ttl ntriples application/n-triples .nt rdfxml application/rdf+xml .rdf jsonld application/ld+json .jsonld

Vitrify chooses the filename extension from the response Content-Type, even when it differs from --format. If that media type is missing or unrecognized, it uses the extension for --format. With neither available, it writes results.dat and prints a warning.

When --format is omitted, Vitrify does not send an Accept header.

Vitrify saves successful response bytes unchanged. The requested format does not guarantee the endpoint returns that media type; use the recorded Content-Type to identify the response.

A non-success HTTP response returns a nonzero exit status and saves the failed retrieval in the RO-Crate metadata, including its error and duration.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: This page describes capabilities being considered for Vitrify. They are planned work, not features of the current CLI, and no delivery dates are set.

docs.title: Planned capabilities
docs.text:
• More retrieval types: retrieve a linked-data representation for an IRI and fetch an arbitrary URL as a local file.
  • Croissant metadata: support Croissant output alongside the current RO-Crate metadata.
  • Additional representations: offer optional raw-response or normalized graph outputs for workflows that need them.

The current CLI supports SPARQL retrieval with vitrify sparql. See the CLI for available options and the RO-Crate output guide for the RO-Crate files it writes today.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Each example shows a saved SPARQL query, a preview of its response, and the files Vitrify wrote. Open a file link in the directory preview to inspect the captured source, response, or RO-Crate metadata.

Query from a file is probably the most production-ready approach: the query can be versioned and reused in a pipeline. The other examples use echo and standard input to keep their commands self-contained.

  • Female Nobel laureates — a CSV result table from Wikidata.
  • EU capitals — five English capital labels in CSV.
  • Query from a file — save the EU-capitals query, then run it with --query query.rq.
  • Top ten metaclasses — metaclasses ranked by direct instance counts.
  • Metaclasses of metaclasses — metaclasses whose recorded instances are all metaclasses, with example instances.
  • Fourth-order classes — all items explicitly typed as fourth-order classes.
  • Time-bounded subclasses — a JSON result table with subclass intervals.
  • SELECT with Turtle requested — a format negotiation example requesting Turtle for a SELECT query.

docs.title: RO-Crate
docs.text:
vitrify sparql --to DIRECTORY writes the result and two evidence files into the directory:

female-persons/
  query.rq
  results.csv
  ro-crate-metadata.json

results.<extension> is the ordinary response body, stored unchanged. Its extension comes from a recognized response Content-Type. If that media type is missing or unrecognized, Vitrify falls back to --format, then to .dat when no format was requested.

query.rq contains the exact query text sent to the endpoint. It is included even when the query was read from standard input.

ro-crate-metadata.json is an RO-Crate 1.2 JSON-LD document describing the retrieval. It links the result and query files and records their byte sizes and SHA-256 checksums, the result media type when provided, the endpoint, response status, final URL, requested Accept value when one was sent, and retrieval times. The retrieval action has a completed or failed status. Linked PropertyValue entities record retrieval duration in seconds. Duration covers the request, redirects, and response download; it excludes final metadata writing.

The result media type describes the received response and can differ from the requested format.

The root dataset's license text says that Vitrify does not assert a license for retrieved data. Check the source endpoint's terms before reusing that data.

Open the complete example metadata file:

RO-Crate metadata for the Wikidata example

docs.title: Reusing an output directory
docs.text:
A successful retrieval into an existing directory overwrites query.rq, the result file with the selected extension, and ro-crate-metadata.json. Result files with other extensions remain: receiving JSON after a previous CSV response leaves both results.json and results.csv, while the new metadata describes only results.json. Use a new directory or preserve the existing capture in version control before retrieving again.

Vitrify initializes the query and metadata before requesting the endpoint. It replaces the metadata atomically when the retrieval finishes. A network or HTTP failure records the error and duration and returns a nonzero exit status. A streaming failure can leave a partial response, identified as incomplete in the metadata rather than linked as a successful result. An interrupted process can leave an active action; treat that capture as incomplete.

Invalid inputs fail before retrieval initialization. If the output directory cannot be written, the CLI reports the filesystem error; a saved attempt may not be available.

docs.title: Example history
docs.text:
Each example has WDQS and QLever tabs, each with its own command, saved files, and response-size history. Select a bar to open that attempt's permanent page. The newest attempt is selected by default, including failures. Hover or focus a bar for its timestamp, outcome, byte count, and duration. A hollow ? marker indicates an unavailable size; bar height represents the saved response size in bytes. Duration appears beneath each bar. Older captures use estimated durations derived from their recorded timestamps, marked with ≈.

From the repository root, with the project environment activated, append a new capture for every example on both endpoints (14 retrievals):

cargo build
j examples

The runner uses the local debug build when available, otherwise vitrify from PATH. It runs the displayed endpoint variants sequentially in temporary directories and saves Vitrify's output in new timestamped directories. Earlier captures stay intact. It continues after individual failures, validates saved crates against RO-Crate 1.2, and exits nonzero if any retrieval or validation failed. Validation results appear in the terminal. Documentation builds read saved captures.
